themes_detail.label: Water System Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints spiked to 37 THIS WEEK, a 362% increase versus the 8-week average of 8 complaints per week (z-score: 5.39), suggesting a acute infrastructure failure or contamination event affecting multiple buildings or blocks in Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: 37 water system complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (362% spike)
Z-score of 5.39 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Concurrent spike in sewer complaints (9 THIS WEEK vs. 2.2 avg, 300% increase) suggests systemic water/waste infrastructure issue
Heat/hot water remains top complaint category (4,038 over 90 days), indicating ongoing utility pressures
reporting_angles: Track DEP response: Are crews responding to localized main breaks or contamination events? Interview residents in affected blocks.
Investigate whether water/sewer spikes correlate geographically—is this one neighborhood or district-wide?

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Detection Surge
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints jumped to 10 LAST WEEK, a 1043% spike versus the 8-week average of 0.9 complaints (z-score: 11.69, highest severity), indicating either a major demolition/renovation project, a building disclosure event, or contamination discovery affecting CD 309.
evidence: 10 asbestos complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly average (1043% spike, highest z-score at 11.69)
DOB shows 321 total permit filings in last 90 days, including 6 full demolitions and 180 alterations—likely triggering abatement work
Asbestos spikes historically precede tenant displacement and health complaints; residents may lack awareness of protections
reporting_angles: Identify which buildings/blocks triggered asbestos complaints—cross-reference with DOB demolition and ALT permits to pinpoint sites.
Interview residents and tenant advocates: Are people being notified of asbestos work? Are they being relocated? Are contractors licensed?

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 31 LAST WEEK, a 351% increase versus the 8-week average of 6.9 per week (z-score: 5.19), suggesting rapid pavement degradation, pothole proliferation, or deferred maintenance across multiple thoroughfares in Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: 31 street condition complaints LAST WEEK vs. 6.9 weekly average (351% spike)
Z-score of 5.19 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Concurrent spike in maintenance/facility complaints (8 LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 avg, 392% increase) suggests broader public infrastructure neglect
Snow/ice complaints remain elevated at 667 over 90 days, indicating seasonal pressures on street maintenance
reporting_angles: Map recent street condition 311 complaints—are they concentrated in one area or district-wide? Visit sites to document potholes, heaves, and deterioration.
Interview DOT: What is the repair timeline? Are they understaffed or underfunded?

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Alert
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, a 256% spike versus the 8-week average of 1.1 per week (z-score: 8.69), suggesting localized pollution, construction dust, or industrial emissions affecting respiratory health in the district.
evidence: 4 air quality complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (256% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Concurrent asbestos spike and street/maintenance surges suggest active construction/demolition work generating dust and emissions
No Reddit or local news coverage yet—story is emerging and underreported
reporting_angles: Correlate air quality complaints with DOB demolition permits (6 filed) and alteration permits (180 filed)—which sites are active?
Interview residents near problem areas: What odors or visible dust are they reporting? Are asthmatic/elderly residents experiencing health impacts?

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Escalate
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints spiked to 22 LAST WEEK, a 214% increase versus the 8-week average of 7.0 per week (z-score: 5.57), and rank third overall in 90-day volume (1,576 total), indicating construction activity, venue overcrowding, or vehicle traffic creating sustained quality-of-life issues.
evidence: 22 noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.0 weekly average (214% spike)
Noise ranks 3rd in 90-day volume at 1,576 complaints—endemic issue with NEW acceleration
Concurrent street/maintenance/asbestos spikes suggest construction activity as primary driver; abandoned vehicle spike (11 THIS WEEK vs. 4.2 avg) may indicate illegal parking and idling noise
reporting_angles: Sample noise complaints filed LAST WEEK—identify recurring locations and times (evenings? weekends? specific blocks?)
Interview NYPD and DOE enforcement: Are construction noise violations being cited? Are nighttime work restrictions enforced?
